metadata.title: The Finance Agent That Cannot Approve Itself
metadata.series: Humanitarians AI Fellows — Weekly Research Reports
metadata.source_status: Real fellow work, actual code and artifacts only. Local deterministic workflow, no external LLM in the runtime. The committed sample review request remains OPEN; no human approval or causal explanation was fabricated.

beats.narration_text: This is Onyx, in for Humanitarians AI. This week on the Mycroft Finance Investigator. By now the agent can compute a verified variance and collect its evidence. So here's the sharp question this week answers in code: should it be allowed to approve its own explanation? The answer is no — and the interesting part is exactly how the system makes that impossible.

beats.narration_text: Act one — the problem. Computing a number is safe. Blessing it is not.

props.title: The Problem — Self-Approval
props.body: Computing a number is safe. Blessing it is not.

beats.narration_text: Start from what already works. On the synthetic sample — forty-three data rows across six datasets — the engine computed a budgeted EBITDA of three hundred fifty thousand against an actual of two hundred thirty thousand: a variance of minus a hundred and twenty thousand. Seven tool steps, forty-one evidence references, every number traced. All of that is verified. None of it is approved.

artifactLines: 43 data rows across six synthetic datasets
7 tool steps · 41 evidence references, every number traced

beats.narration_text: Here's the trap. If the agent that produced those numbers were also allowed to sign off on why they happened, the human-control boundary would be gone. The same system would make the claim and bless it. Calculating the bridge is a math problem. Deciding it's acceptable, and why, is a judgment — and this week that judgment is fenced off.

props.sparkLine: Don't let the author grade the exam.
props.heading: Why a gate at all
props.body: If the agent could approve its own explanation, one system would both make the claim and bless it. Computing the variance is a math problem; deciding it is acceptable is a human judgment.
props.evidenceNote: The boundary is enforced in code, not policy.

beats.narration_text: Act two — the review gate, in review dot py.

props.title: The Review Gate
props.body: review.py — a request the agent can open, but only a human can clear.

beats.narration_text: The investigator's only move is to open a request. It stamps the exact run — the run ID and a SHA-256 hash of the run log — sets the gate status to OPEN, and leaves the reviewer name deliberately blank. The file even carries its own instructions: a named human completes this; the investigator cannot approve itself.

props.title: review.py — build_review_request()
props.sparkLine: The agent can only open the gate.

beats.narration_text: Four rules stand between an open request and a cleared one. It's bound to the run, by ID and hash. It rejects agent identities, and any evidence the run never collected. Approval has to be earned — a human materiality decision plus an evidence-backed cause. And once a decision is recorded, it's written once. No overwrites.

layers.sub: carries the run ID + a SHA-256 of the run log

layers.title: No agent, no unknown evidence
layers.sub: agent identities rejected; every citation must exist in the run

layers.title: APPROVE is earned

layers.title: Append-only
layers.sub: a recorded decision is written once; overwrite refused

beats.narration_text: Here is the enforcement, verbatim. There's a set of known agent identities. If the reviewer name matches one of them, the gate raises an error: the investigator or another agent cannot clear a human gate. And to APPROVE at all, the materiality threshold must be approved or replaced, and there must be at least one evidence-backed causal explanation. Miss either, and approval is refused.

props.title: review.py — the enforcement
props.sparkLine: The agent's name is on the deny-list.

beats.narration_text: The shape of a valid decision isn't left to chance either — it's pinned by a JSON schema. A decision names the run, the reviewer, and a timestamp. It picks one verdict: approve, request changes, or block. It states a materiality decision. And every causal explanation it lists has to cite at least one piece of evidence.

artifactLines: causal_explanations[] — each cites at least one evidence reference

beats.narration_text: Act three — does it actually hold?

props.title: The Gate Holds
props.body: Watch the self-approval attempt fail — then the human gate clear.

beats.narration_text: Two commands. First, review-request opens the gate — status OPEN, bound to the run. Then the agent tries to record its own approval, signing as the investigator. The gate refuses: an agent cannot clear a human gate. Only when a named human supplies the decision, with an evidence-backed cause, does it clear — and that record is written once, append-only.

artifactLines: review-request  →  review gate: OPEN  (bound to run + SHA-256)
record-review · reviewer "mycroft-finance-investigator"  →  ReviewError: an agent cannot clear a human gate
record-review · a named human + evidence  →  gate: CLEARED, recorded append-only
props.sparkLine: The machine asks. The human decides.

beats.narration_text: None of this is a promise — it's tested. Seven new review-control tests: the request opens bound to the run's hash; an agent identity is rejected; approve demands a causal explanation; unknown evidence is rejected; a recorded decision is append-only; and the decision must match the run. With the finance suite, that's nineteen tests passing this week.

props.heading: Proven, not promised
props.body: Seven new review-control tests — open-and-bound, agent rejected, approval needs a cause, unknown evidence rejected, append-only, decision must match the run. Nineteen passing this week.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. This is a local, deterministic workflow — no external model in the runtime. The review request is bound to the exact run by ID and SHA-256; agent identities and unknown evidence are rejected; approval requires a human materiality decision and an evidence-backed cause; and recorded decisions are append-only. And to be clear about this week's artifact: the committed sample review request is still OPEN. No human approval, and no causal explanation, was fabricated to close it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. This week's gate stops a finance agent from approving itself. But approving is only half the risk — publishing is the other half. So think about it, and answer in the comments: what controls would you require before allowing a finance agent to publish its findings?
